title: Ensure 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services' is set to 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users' (MS only)
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 2.2.10: Ensure 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services' is set to 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users' (MS only)

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Check if Remote Desktop Services is installed
steps.function: 1. Check if Remote Desktop Services (TermService) is installed and running. Use read-only PowerShell to query the service status; changed_when: false; failed_when: rc not in [0, 1].

steps.name: Evaluate service presence
steps.function: 2. Evaluate whether Remote Desktop Services is installed and running. If not installed or not running, set _cis_status to SKIP and jump to step-06. Otherwise continue to step-03.

computations._cis_status: SKIP if _service_status is empty or not 'Running', otherwise continue

steps.name: Read current value of 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services'
steps.function: 3. Read current value of 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services'. Use read-only PowerShell to query the current value; changed_when: false; failed_when: rc not in [0, 1].

parameters.cmd: secedit /export /areas USER_RIGHTS /cfg C:\Windows\Temp\cis_audit_2_2_10.inf | Out-Null; $content = Get-Content C:\Windows\Temp\cis_audit_2_2_10.inf; $line = $content | Where-Object { $_ -match 'SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight' }; if ($line) { $line } else { '** FAIL **' }

steps.name: Evaluate whether 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services' is equals 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users'
steps.function: 4. Evaluate whether 'Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services' is equals 'Administrators, Remote Desktop Users'. PASS if compliant, FAIL if not, SKIP if not applicable, ERROR if failed.

computations._cis_status: PASS if audit output contains '** PASS **', FAIL if '** FAIL **', SKIP otherwise

steps.name: Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result'
steps.function: 5. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

steps.name: Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg
steps.function:
6. Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg with EXACTLY this format:
AUDIT REPORT — CIS 2.2.10
Reference: CIS Benchmark checkpoint 2.2.10
Then for each requirement: REQUIREMENT NN - {{ req_NN }}:
  With fields: Task, Command, Exit code, Data, Status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR), Details.
End with OVERALL COMPLIANCE: section containing Result: {{{ cis_result }}}

steps.name: Emit compliance result
steps.function: Output the overall compliance status to the caller.

steps.name: Handle task failure
steps.function: Reached via rescue block on any unexpected task failure.

phases.description: Apply remediation changes on the target host.

phases.name: Analysis
phases.description: Evaluate collected data and determine compliance status.

phases.name: Reporting
phases.description: Emit the compliance result to the caller.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
Any task failure (collect or action step) is routed to the abort handler (step-08) which reports ERROR.
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
